name: chicken salad
instructions:
A french-forward chicken salad — chicken + mayo + dijon + chicken broth food-processed into a smooth base, then folded with tarragon + dill + raw celery + apple + raisins/cranberries + lemon. The food processor is load-bearing here (see notes) — hand-shredding doesn't work for this specific dish even though it works for other chicken preparations.

SERVES 4-6.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

Smooth base (food processor):
- 2-3 cups cooked chicken (poached, roasted, or rotisserie), rough-chopped
- 1/3 to 1/2 cup mayonnaise (adjust to preference)
- 1-2 tbsp DIJON MUSTARD (not optional — see notes)
- 2-3 tbsp chicken broth (a small amount; see notes)
- salt and black pepper to taste

Fold-ins (added at the end, NOT processed):
- 2-3 stalks celery, finely diced
- 1 apple, finely diced (skin on)
- 1/4 cup raisins AND/OR dried cranberries (either or both — hard to clash)
- 1-2 tbsp fresh tarragon, finely chopped
- 1-2 tbsp fresh dill, finely chopped
- squeeze of lemon juice (~1 tbsp)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. FOOD PROCESSOR — SMOOTH BASE: add the cooked chicken, mayonnaise, dijon mustard, and chicken broth to a food processor. Season with salt and pepper. Process until the chicken breaks down into a smooth, spreadable paste-like base (~30-60 seconds, scrape down as needed). This is the load-bearing step (see notes) — the finished salad should read as one cohesive spread, not chunky.

2. TRANSFER TO A BOWL. The base should be creamy and cohesive, holding together like a spread.

3. FOLD IN THE RAW VEGETABLE/FRUIT ITEMS: add the finely diced celery, diced apple, raisins and/or cranberries, chopped tarragon, chopped dill, and lemon juice. Fold with a spatula until evenly distributed. Don't over-mix — the fold-ins should stay visually distinct against the smooth base.

4. TASTE + ADJUST: check salt, pepper, and lemon. Chill 30 min before serving to let flavors meld (optional but improves).

5. SERVE: on bread as a sandwich (croissants, brioche, whole-grain toast); on crackers; on top of greens; in a lettuce wrap. Keeps ~3 days in the fridge.
notes:
French-forward chicken salad with tarragon + dill as the herb pair, dijon mustard mandatory, and the crucial food-processor step for the base.

=== FOOD PROCESSOR STEP IS LOAD-BEARING — HAND-SHREDDING DOESN'T WORK HERE ===

Most chicken salads shred or dice the chicken by hand. That approach doesn't work for this recipe — the finished salad reads as separate chicken pieces sitting in mayo rather than a cohesive spread, and the mustard + broth don't distribute evenly. THIS DISH SPECIFICALLY NEEDS THE FOOD PROCESSOR TO PULVERIZE THE CHICKEN + MAYO + MUSTARD + BROTH INTO A SMOOTH BASE first, then the raw fold-ins go in after by hand.

CROSS-REFERENCE — when hand-shred DOES work (and when it doesn't):
- HAND-SHRED WORKS for [[chicken-pot-pie]] and other cooked-chicken applications where the chicken is a chunky filling in a sauce.
- HAND-SHRED WORKS for [[egg-salad]] where the eggs mash naturally with a fork into a chunky-but-cohesive texture.
- HAND-SHRED DOESN'T WORK HERE because chicken meat doesn't have the natural mash-together character of egg yolks; without the food processor pulverizing it, the chicken stays as discrete strands / chunks that don't bind with the mayo-mustard-broth base into one spread.

The food processor is what makes this dish specifically read as a smooth french-style chicken salad rather than a chunky american-style deli chicken salad. Not interchangeable.

=== CHICKEN BROTH — SMALL AMOUNT, INTO THE PROCESSOR ===

2-3 tbsp chicken broth goes into the food processor with the chicken, mayo, and mustard. Small amount — you're not making chicken soup. The broth does two things:
1. LOOSENS THE BASE so it processes smoothly without being just mayo-dense
2. REINFORCES THE CHICKEN FLAVOR — the broth adds concentrated chicken character back into the base that the cooked chicken alone loses during processing

Without the broth the food-processed base reads dry and mayo-forward; with it, the base has real chicken depth.

=== MAYO + DIJON MUSTARD ARE BOTH NON-OPTIONAL ===

Both ALWAYS in — pick-one isn't a valid approach here:
- MAYO: the fat + creamy body carrier. Mayo alone would read too round and flat.
- DIJON MUSTARD: the tang + savory depth carrier. Dijon alone would read too sharp and thin.
Together they lock the base into the right cream-and-tang register — same principle as [[french-lentil-salad]]'s cream + mustard + vinegar vinaigrette (mustard + acid + fat, all three needed).

=== TARRAGON + DILL AS THE HERB PAIR ===

Both fresh herbs are primary. Tarragon carries the french anise-forward register; dill adds a brighter grassy note that complements without competing. Together they're the herb signature of this dish.

Don't sub dried tarragon or dried dill — the dried versions read wrong here (concentrated and slightly bitter, competes with the mayo). Fresh only.

=== FOLD-INS ARE FLEXIBLE — CELERY + APPLE + RAISINS/CRANBERRIES ARE ALL FINE ===

The raw fold-ins are hard to mess up in this dish:
- CELERY: finely diced. Traditional in most chicken salads; crunchy contrast against the smooth base.
- APPLE: finely diced, skin on. Sweet-crisp counterpoint. Any variety works; slightly tart (granny smith, honeycrisp) reads best.
- RAISINS AND/OR DRIED CRANBERRIES: either or both. Sweet-chewy pops throughout. Hard to clash — the sweet fruit sits cleanly against the dijon and herbs.

All three together works fine. Pick just apple, or just raisins, or all-of-the-above — the dish tolerates the variation.

=== NO CUCUMBERS ===

Cucumbers were previously listed as an ingredient — removed. They add too much water to a spread that wants to hold its shape and don't earn their place against the herbs and dried fruit. If you want a crunchy fresh element, celery covers that slot cleanly.

=== CHICKEN COOKING METHOD — ANY WORKS ===

Poached chicken (classic french technique — gentle water simmer with aromatics) gives the cleanest flavor and moistest texture. Roasted chicken breast works. Rotisserie chicken is the shortcut and produces a fine result — the food processor + mayo + broth carry enough flavor that the chicken cook method matters less than you'd think.

=== FAILURE MODES ===

Two real ways this dish goes wrong:

1. FORGOT THE LEMON JUICE. Easy to miss — the lemon goes in with the raw fold-ins near the end and it's a small quantity (~1 tbsp) buried in a longer ingredient list. Skipping it leaves the finished salad noticeably flat — the mayo + dijon + broth base is rich but savory-monotone; the lemon is what brightens it. If you catch the miss after tasting, stir it in at the end; the dish recovers.

2. TOO MUCH OR TOO LITTLE CHICKEN BROTH. The broth quantity is small (2-3 tbsp) but load-bearing:
   - TOO MUCH BROTH: base processes into a wet paste that doesn't hold shape on bread/tortilla, and the mayo-to-broth ratio tips watery. Slides off the spread rather than holding together.
   - TOO LITTLE BROTH: base processes dry and dense; the food processor struggles to break the chicken down smoothly, and the finished base reads mayo-heavy without the chicken depth the broth was supposed to reinforce.
   Start at 2 tbsp; add 1 more tbsp if the processor is struggling; don't go past 3 tbsp without good reason.

=== SERVING — TORTILLAS ARE THE BEST FORMAT ===

TORTILLAS (flour or spinach) are the best way to eat this. The food-processed spread holds together perfectly wrapped in a tortilla — no messy fall-out like a bread sandwich, easy to eat one-handed, and the tortilla's neutral character lets the herb + fruit + chicken flavors lead.

Other valid serving formats (all secondary to the tortilla wrap):
- On bread (croissants for the classical french presentation, brioche for softer, whole-grain toast for heartier)
- On crackers
- On top of a green salad
- In a lettuce wrap (lower-carb alternative to the tortilla)

Keeps ~3 days in the fridge — the food-processed base doesn't degrade the way discrete chicken chunks might.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[egg-salad]]: uses hand-mashing rather than a food processor (egg yolks have natural bind that chicken doesn't).
- [[chicken-pot-pie]]: uses hand-shredded chicken — different application entirely (chunks in sauce, not a spread).
- [[french-lentil-salad]]: shares the mustard + acid + creamy fat vinaigrette philosophy (dijon + white wine vinegar + cream, all three).
